54: Two photos do it: the worst ripple up close, then the whole room from the doorway. An estimator reads them and answers in writing that same business day — $99 stretch, or replacement, with the price either way. No van comes up the driveway, and nobody calls to sell you anything.

69: Cottage Lake sits off the retail map, which is exactly the address this van was built for. Gravel, a hill, a quarter mile of trees — it comes up the driveway anyway, carrying 20+ carpet samples aboard and all three pad grades with them. Samples go down in whichever rooms are being replaced, so the color reads under your own light. Every room and stair gets measured, the written price stays behind, and the visit itself is free.
71: Ripples usually show up first in the long hallways and daylight-basement rec rooms these houses are built around. Restretching in Cottage Lake starts at $99 per room. A power stretcher takes out waves, buckles and trip edges for roughly a fifth of replacement cost, so while the pile is healthy and the color still suits you, that's the cheaper answer.
79: Four things end a carpet's life: traffic lanes crushed flat, seams pulling apart, backing breaking down, or pet odor that survived professional cleaning. Any one of those, and stretching just delays it. None of them — pile still standing, backing sound, a color you can live with — and a $99-per-room stretch does the job instead of a new floor. Out on the acreage lots it's often one hard-used room gone and the rest merely loose. We look before we quote.
83: Horse properties, muddy dogs and the occasional barn boot set the bar out here. What clears it: a moisture-barrier pad underneath, a sealed backing above that, and solution-dyed nylon on top. The first two stop accidents before they reach the subfloor, which is where odor turns permanent; the third takes a diluted-bleach scrub without losing color. Moving up to the barrier pad starts at $0.65 per square foot.
85: Start with the pad, since it can decide whether the mill honors anything — one more reason all three pad grades ride out in the van. Then two coverages: the mill's on the carpet, usually 10 to 25 years against wear and stain depending on the grade you choose, and OC Flooring's own 1-year workmanship warranty on the install. Both land on your written quote, which is what people out here read before signing.
